DIMENSIONAL_TRAVELER_EVENT_UNSEALED_RECO:
Beyond a half-buried stone door, a stack of records still turns its own pages.

Every page preserves the same failure: treating change as something that can be carried away.

The reactions along the paper's edge grow quiet as you approach. They recognize this vessel, but not your right to decide what happens next.

You press the record back into the chamber behind the stone door and mark the range in which it still reacts.

Containment is not erasure. Whoever opens it later will still know that something was left here.

You do not decide how it should be handled. You give over both the record and its boundary.

They do not promise to seal it forever. They only offer a tool enough to continue the road.

You use a portion of the vessel to steady the reaction on the page.

The record yields rare materials that have lost their former use. The pain remains in the vessel; the materials remain in your hand.

Beyond a half-buried stone door, a stack of records still turns its own pages.

The symbols belong to no writing you recognize, but whenever a page turns, the rubble beyond the door briefly changes shape.

This is no relic that will wait quietly to be found.

You take nothing from the record and wait outside until its unstable reactions settle.

A lingering warmth closes your wounds for a while.

You do not understand all of it. You copy only one fragment, enough to change how you make your next move.

Copying is not mastery.

You remove the fragments that are still reacting and trade them for material value.

The record does not disappear. It only leaves behind a sharper, more dangerous edge.
